note: The window address of the self-dispatched flowEvalTick chain, declared as data — for BOTH surfaces of this subset, which run the one shared chain (`🧵️preview-eval`). `arming` is what a surface's pending_effects may put on the wire for a given attached-window roster; `dispatch` is which of those addresses that surface's retained route admits. Each row names the `surface` it governs (`editor` | `viewer`). Language-agnostic: an implementation in any language must answer these exact rows.

arming.why: Before the first SurfaceVisible there is no roster and no window transient to publish into — the chain waits instead of spinning an address that cannot land.
The flow window holds no evaluation publication; arming a tick it can only refuse is the served-app stall.
The preview window owns the retained evaluation, so the tick names it — never the current window.
Every preview window holds its OWN publication, so every one gets its own addressed chain.
Generate preview owns the same retained evaluation chain as edit preview, addressed at its own window id.
The read-only surface obeys the same law: before the first SurfaceVisible there is no window transient to publish into, so nothing is armed.
The viewer's single preview window owns the retained evaluation, so the tick names it — the chain is not editor-only.

dispatch.why: The defect: an Effect::DispatchAction carries no window, so the shell redispatches under the current window and the route refuses.
An attached window of the wrong KIND is refused, not silently accepted.
The fix: the payload names the preview window, so the runtime captures THAT window's transient authority while the shell stays focused on the flow window.
A window that left the roster fails closed — the chain ends and the next refresh re-arms it, rather than spinning.
The generate preview tick is window-scoped: the payload names generation3d-generate-preview while the shell stays on the generations list.
An unaddressed tick is refused on the read-only surface too, even though its preview window happens to be the current one — the address is the payload's, never the shell's focus.
The fix: the payload names the viewer preview window, so the runtime captures THAT window's transient authority and the brep round trip can publish into it.
A window that left the roster fails closed — the chain ends and the next refresh re-arms it, rather than spinning.
